answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity costly to maintain: every agent must lock a stake and tend a reputation orchard, where good attestations grow trust slowly while one bad act burns the stake. Like a jetty holding back the tide, fresh identities start with zero weight, so an attacker must pay real stake and time for each fake agent, and the cost of forging many identities quickly exceeds any gain from flooding votes or claims.
